data.title: Israelis, Palestinians must 'reboot relations': Absence of diplomatic route means 'perpetual war'
data.description: Mark Owen is pleased to welcome Yossi Mekelberg, Senior Consulting Fellow of the Middle East and North Africa Programme at Chatham House. Can Israel continue to define its future primarily through security and territorial control? Mekelberg challenges the notion that military operations, incursions and settlement expansion can constitute a sustainable political objective. He identifies a potential transition beyond the Netanyahu era as an opportunity to reconsider the relationship between Israeli and Palestinian societies. His central argument is that the continuation of war without a political endgame risks a state of perpetual conflict.

data.title: ‘They accepted the money but didn’t take care of my child’: what Luna Wong’s death reveals about the treatment of international students in the UK
data.description: When her parents waved her off to study in England they hoped it would be a fresh start the 16-year-old needed after struggling with her mental health in Hong Kong. Instead, 10 months later, she was dead. What went so wrong? As a young teen, one of Luna Wong’s favourite things to do was to walk to a bridge near her home in Hong Kong and sit there for a while, listening to the traffic and the water below, looking out at the lights and the activity of the city. She had a particular way of observing the world, which she expressed through photography. Her pictures were mostly landscapes, ordinary corners of Hong Kong, but she could spot an image nobody else would have seen in the same place. She was an inquisitive kid who enjoyed making people laugh, and was deeply interested in the world around her. Then in 2019, when she was 13, political unrest in Hong Kong , swiftly followed by Covid lockdowns, shrank that world to the size of her bedroom. For a prolonged period, Luna barely left her family’s flat. School became a screen; friends were only accessible virtually. She stopped sleeping properly, started having panic attacks, and was diagnosed with depression and anxiety. When the world opened up after Covid, Luna was too changed to step easily back into it. She was often so anxious she couldn’t attend school, and fell seriously behind. Her psychiatrist prescribed antidepressants, anti-anxiety medication and sleeping pills. Later, ADHD medication and an anti-psychotic drug were added to the mix. This heavy combination of prescription drugs left her lethargic in the day – though still often awake at night – and caused weight gain, which distressed her. But Luna retained her curious streak. Keen to understand her own issues better, she read about psychology, ordering textbooks to teach herself about the human mind. When her friends had problems, she offered advice, and dreamed of becoming a psychologist. But it was hard to see how this would be possible as she struggled to attend school. Continue reading...

data.title: Look again – there’s more to Germany’s election trends than far-right success | Cas Mudde
data.description: Defeatist narratives abound. Yet Germany’s latest elections suggest voter dissatisfaction is benefiting the left as well as the right Germany held three regional elections this month and, although each of them had a unique result, much of the media and political commentary reduced them to: “ German chancellor clings to power after latest loss to far right . Since 2016, the year of Brexit and Trump, “embattled mainstream threatened by emboldened far right” has become the overarching narrative about Europe. But while these elections were important, this reductive take both oversimplifies the complexities of contemporary European politics and drives a defeatist “ end of democracy ” narrative. Saxony-Anhalt’s election on 6 September was a global news event – understandably, given Germany’s history, economy and place in Europe. The international media had speculated for months about an outright majority for the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD). The party came close, setting a record score with 43.8%, but it has so far failed to form a government, despite the amenable position of the “left-conservative” Sahra Wagenknecht Alliance. Continue reading...

data.title: How drawn-out saga of Manchester City’s alleged cheating came to this
data.description: Club’s ruthless approach was always at odds with their public image and this inglorious story has further to run There is no episode in English football’s history that even resembles a precedent for the epic Manchester City disciplinary drama, which encapsulates the modern game at breaking point. Here was a grand, stoic old club, taken over in 2008 by Abu Dhabi royalty and mega-funded to imperious success, then crowned serial champions by a league simultaneously pursuing charges of monstrous financial cheating. On Friday sources confirmed that saga, in which Pep Guardiola’s expensively constructed City teams won five Premier League titles and the Champions League during the years since the investigation began in December 2018, culminated in guilty findings on almost all of more than 100 charges. Continue reading...

data.title: Lamine Yamal: ‘Football is mechanised but players like me have that special spark’
data.description: Spain and Barcelona wonderkid has won World Cup and European Championship but says there are no limits for his career Like the kid he is, Lamine Yamal just wanted to keep playing. This wasn’t Plaça Joan XXIII, wasn’t El Parque de Rocafonda either; it wasn’t the Mataró neighbourhood where it all began, but it might have been. “We’re in a World Cup final and I wanted to carry on,” he says, and there’s the smile again, the braces. Really? “Yes”. No nerves? “No. I never thought: ‘Just blow the whistle’. I was enjoying it.” No fear, just fun: 19 July, New Jersey and he knew: this 19-year-old who had happily been asleep on the bus to the biggest match of his life. And now he sits in a first-floor office in Las Rozas, surrounded by tactics boards and stats sheets. There’s a Spain keyring hanging from the door and a second star on his shirt. In the corridor, crates loaded for London. Son of Mounir and Sheila, named after the family friends who helped them, “ touched by God’s wand ” in the words of the coach whose office is next door, there’s something about Lamine Yamal. He turned 17 the day before the final of Euro 2024 , a schoolboy sitting exams, and 19 the day before the semi-final of the World Cup. Asked what he wanted, he said a trip to New York, so there he was, about to be a champion again. Continue reading...

data.title: Cooking with Tom Kerridge, the Michelin ‘meatfluencer’
data.description: The star chef demystified the restaurant scene with his love of a welcoming pub. Now he explains why hospitality is in crisis – and how to make a sublime venison chilli Tom Kerridge is the king of meat: first as a chef, transforming pub classics like pork belly into Michelin-starred fare at The Hand and Flowers in Marlow 20 years ago, and later opening The Butcher’s Tap and Grill in the same village; then as a cookery writer: his Outdoor Cooking – The Ultimate Modern Barbecue Bible of 2021 is well named, being both as comprehensive and as worshipful as a holy book; and recently as a “meat-fluencer”, making gorgeous skills videos on Instagram and YouTube . That was just destiny, he says (more or less). “When you’re cooking in a classic brigade system, the sections are like a larder: you’ve got starters, you’ve got garnish, you’ve got meat and fish, you’ve got pastry. The meat is the lead section, where the most experienced chef is, because that’s where you land when you’ve learned to treat vegetables with love and respect. If you fuck up cabbage, it doesn’t cost a lot.” It’s true, it doesn’t, but if you saw the care Kerridge puts into dicing an onion – peeling its layers apart like he’s making a mosaic, assiduous even about half an inch of waste – of an onion – you’d know that love and respect aren’t really about money. Continue reading...

data.title: Kyiv has become a frontline city - and winter is on the way
data.description: Residents of Ukraine’s capital prepare for power cuts, drones and bitter cold by stocking up on generators, food and ‘dry showers’ It felt like the last day of summer. On a Sunday afternoon in late September, people in Kyiv strolled through the city’s botanical gardens, admiring the late-flowering dahlias. Later, the terraces in the Podil area – a neighbourhood full of bars, patisseries and bookshops – filled up with customers in search of a cocktail. The idyll was an illusion. As the day darkened, the air defence began its rumble and boom. When a projectile fell with an explosive smack on a bar table, the drinkers flinched and then laughed. It was only a conker from the chestnut tree overhead. Nursing a glass of rosé, writer Myroslav Laiuk talked about the picnic he and his wife had had the previous evening, in a park in the Obolon district – prosecco in proper glasses, cheese and charcuterie. Then a drone was shot down above their heads. Very pretty, he said, with a smile. Shooting stars. Time to make a wish. Continue reading...

data.title: Trump faces tough choices as Iran dangles deal to reopen Hormuz before US midterms
data.description: Iran’s seven-day timetable would restart nuclear talks, but will the US be willing to deliver on terms that include reining in Israel in Lebanon? Iran’s seven-day timetable to reopen the strait of Hormuz and start talks on its nuclear programme has been pitched as a deal that could rapidly extricate Donald Trump from a political crisis but requires the US president to make difficult concessions. In the five days left before the proposed reopening of the strait, which is expected to relieve pressure on global energy markets, Trump would need to lift Iranian asset freezes, permit Iran to export its oil and, probably most difficult of all, order Benjamin Netanyahu to end Israel’s attacks on Hezbollah in Lebanon, thus achieving the “ceasefire on all fronts”. data.title: ‘We left Ireland because there wasn’t work – and we wanted to get the hell away’: Trespasses author Louise Kennedy
data.description: Her Troubles-set debut became a hit TV series starring Gillian Anderson. Now the novelist has returned to her teen years for a follow-up. She talks about her journey from chef to author, and how her cancer diagnosis inspired her to write Louise Kennedy’s life has hardly wanted for dramatic events, but the recent past has been spectacularly busy, even by her standards. You wouldn’t know it to look at her, as we chat in the sitting room of the house in Sligo that she shares with her husband, son and daughter, but this is the home that she once thought would be repossessed. The couple bought it “for stupid money” in 2007, when they also opened a restaurant, initially so successful that the only way seemed to be up. The following year, financial mayhem descended on Ireland, their customers ebbed away, and the Celtic Tiger years morphed into a country racked with job losses, bankruptcies, apparently endless debt. “I didn’t think I’d ever be able to keep the house,” she says, glancing around an elegant room dotted with beautiful objects and plants, but nonetheless relaxed and comfortable. “I’d say we only got out of negative equity about a month ago. There are probably arguments for moving now, but I’m so proud that we managed to hold on to it, I’m not going anywhere. I’m going to be carried out of here in a box.” Kennedy had been a chef for 30 years, working all over the place from Dublin to London and, for two years, Beirut, before ending up in Sligo, on Ireland’s west coast, not far from the border with her native Northern Ireland. Crucially, she had never given a thought to writing, not since a teacher had admired a poem she wrote when she was seven. Now, she is about to publish her second novel, Stations, which follows a collection of short stories, The End of the World Is a Cul-de-Sac, and her debut, Trespasses, which was shortlisted for the 2023 Women’s prize for fiction and won other prizes in Ireland and the UK in 2022 and 2023. Last year, Trespasses gained further acclaim when it was adapted for Channel 4 in a production starring Gillian Anderson as the mother of Cushla, the young Catholic teacher who falls in love with Michael, an older, married Protestant lawyer, in 1970s Belfast. Continue reading...

data.title: The Guide #262: Why laughing at the movies isn’t always funny
data.description: In this week’s newsletter: From A Space Odyssey to The Exorcist II, audiences can turn a serious film into an accidental comedy – but where does the line fall between laughing with a film, and laughing at it? Before every screening at the West End’s Prince Charles Cinema, a public service message is played. It’s usually one read by John Waters , welcoming cinemagoers to the “most depraved and beautiful movie theatre in London”, before imploring them to “turn off your cellphone, asshole”. More recently, though, a new message has been played, read by none other than Timothée Chalamet, who made a guest appearance at the cinema last year. Along with the usual requests for phones to be switched off, Timmy makes an unusual plea: for audience members not to laugh “like Max Cady” at moments in the film that aren’t supposed to be laughed at. Because the Prince Charles mostly plays older movies, there can be what Chalamet calls a “disconnect” between the time that the film was made and today: ropey scenes of sex or violence, outdated language or technology, or anything else that jars with modern sensibilities and causes people to hoot derisively. It’s a surprisingly real problem, not just at the Prince Charles but at any repertory cinema. On Reddit there are plenty of threads bemoaning people guffawing at everything from A Space Odyssey to the films of David Lynch , a phenomenon one film writer on Substack has christened ‘ performative laughter ’. For anyone caught in a cinema when this unwelcome cackling occurs, it can be a killer. There’s little more guaranteed to break the spell of a non-comedy film than laughter: scary movies are instantly made about 75% less scary, thrillers become less white-knuckle, dramas lose their weight. Continue reading...

data.title: We Manchester City fans fear relegation and losing trophies … but club are bang to rights
data.description: Despite attempts to legally filibuster the charges out of existence for the past three years, we’ve rightfully failed It couldn’t have been more prophetic. In 2008, 15 years before Manchester City were charged with financial fraud, fans started singing “City’s going down with a billion in the bank” to the tune of Yellow Submarine. This was because the former Thailand president Thaksin Shinawatra’s 15-month ownership of City had come to an abrupt end when more than £1bn of his assets were frozen . And although Sheikh Mansour of the UAE had stepped in to save City, we were sinking fast. Despite the UAE’s untold riches, by December we were in the relegation zone. It’s called Cityitis – shorthand for our tendency to self-destruct when things appear to be going well. In fact we won trophy after trophy. But we continued to sing the song about going down with a billion in the bank. When the financial fair play investigation was launched in 2018, the chant got louder. Then in 2023 we learned there were more than 100 charges . The chant became even louder and more cavalier. And now that our grubby, griftin’, cheatin’ chicken has come home to roost , you can bank on one thing (if banks still deal with us) – the chanting will be louder and more cavalier than ever. Continue reading...

data.title: Of course you can be English if you’re not white. So why can’t the right leave the question alone? | Jason Okundaye
data.description: Even Jacob Rees-Mogg pushes back on defining Englishness in exclusively ethnic terms. But the endurance of this discourse is still deeply troubling Can you be English and non-white? It’s a question that keeps stubbornly resurfacing in our political discourse. Last weekend, the former prime minister Rishi Sunak gave his view in a column in the Times, arguing that national identity should not be turned into a DNA test. After leaving office, Sunak, the UK’s first prime minister of colour , was subject to claims by a prominent podcaster that he was not English because he was a “brown-skinned Hindu” . Reflecting on this, Sunak described it as a “reverse Tebbit test ”: the sociological concept measuring the loyalty of immigrants – and their children – in the UK depending on which cricket team they supported in international matches. “Once we say that this or that person isn’t really English or British because they are not white,” he wrote, “then we are on a very slippery slope. Some people will argue that English is an ethnic identity and British a civic identity. Though if you think those nuances are heard by most people, I fear you are being rather – perhaps even wilfully – naive.” Jason Okundaye is an assistant Opinion editor at the Guardian Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? If you would like to submit a response of up to 300 words by email to be considered for publication in our letters section, please click here . Continue reading...

data.description: The French president’s resolve seems to have rubbed off on the leaders of other ‘middle powers’ On the first day of the United Nations general assembly this week, two world leaders outlined competing visions for the future. Donald Trump’s speech was disturbingly familiar to those he’s given before: a litany of false boasts and odd tangents, peppered with grim military threats against a variety of nation states. data.title: Tim Dowling: I’ve been replaced by a younger model … it’s a relief
data.description: My wife has summarily dismissed me from outdoor duties, in favour of ‘Gardening Steve’. Inevitably, there’s a catch My wife wants to hire someone to put the garden in order. She knows I’ll object, because it’s really something I should be doing, but she also knows I won’t do it. In truth, I’ve lost heart. Two scorching months without rain wreaked havoc on the garden: the lawn turned the colour of a winter sky; seedlings vaporised; established shrubs died. When the rains finally came, the garden bounced back – but by then I didn’t care any more. As part of her campaign my wife has let it be known that paying someone to fix the garden is no reflection on me, because I’m a businessman with little time to devote to things of the soil. data.title: It’s not hypothetical: the dangers of AI are already here | Granate Kim and Mohamed Hussein
data.description: Israel and the US have used AI to kill in Gaza and Iran, while law enforcement uses it in surveillance and arrests. The future is here In recent weeks, concerns about AI have forged unlikely alliances in the tech and policy worlds. Tech moguls such as Sam Altman, Elon Musk and Demis Hassabis joined Dario Amodei, Satya Nadella and Bill Gates in sounding the alarm about the dangers of AI and called for a slowdown of the technology’s development despite years of racing for dominance. The senator Bernie Sanders teamed up with Steve Bannon to urge Congress to regulate AI, which has become one of the very few issues to unite Americans across the political spectrum. The latest moves were sparked in part by the AI researcher Jacob Coxon’s warnings on Twitter/X that AI companies are “gambling with our lives” and believe that the technology “could kill us all by the end of the decade”. data.title: The Guardian view on Trump and Xi: a show of friendship, but no real attempt to address the tensions | Editorial
data.description: The Chinese leader’s visit to Washington appears to have done nothing to shift the stalemate in bilateral relations Within days, two high-profile Chinese visitors will arrive in the US – envoys of friendship, as Xi Jinping described them when he met Donald Trump at the White House this week. The giant pandas, Ping Ping and Fu Shuang, will be hosted at Atlanta zoo. Beijing dispatched the first panda pair to the US in 1972 following President Richard Nixon’s landmark visit to China. It uses the animals to indicate satisfaction or displeasure with other nations. But it also charges heftily for their lease: reportedly, around $1m a year per pair. Americans’ views of China have warmed from a pandemic nadir, but are unlikely to be shifted much by two animals, however charming. These days they are more of a token gesture than a striking symbol. It is telling that the announcement was one of the main takeaways of Mr Xi’s visit to Washington . Expectations were low after May’s stalemate summit in Beijing, but this meeting still struggled to meet them. The US president gave Mr Xi a lavish welcome – unusually, travelling to meet the “strong, vibrant and fit” Chinese leader off the plane. He insisted that they had “never gotten along better”. Continue reading...

data.description: All the contenders for this year’s prize are a reflection of the crisis in masculinity Jarvis Cocker, one of the judges for this year’s Booker prize, has expressed surprise that the shortlist , announced this week, contains four male authors and only two female writers, because, “generally speaking, the male-written books weren’t as good as the ones written by women”. The Pulp frontman might be on to something. Over the past 10 years, however, seven Booker winners have been men; the number of women boosted to four by the controversial joint win between Bernardine Evaristo and Margaret Atwood in 2019. The 2024 Booker shortlist was the first to have five female authors in the prize’s history. Last year’s winner Flesh , by British-Hungarian author David Szalay, stripped what being a man means down to its bones. Continue reading...

data.title: Carlos Alcaraz leads by example as Europe take early lead in Laver Cup
data.description: Europe lead Team World 3-1 after opening day Alcaraz wins doubles match with Jakub Mensik By the time Casper Ruud had completed his typically tenacious comeback to capture victory in the opening scuffle of this year’s Laver Cup, Carlos Alcaraz was on the floor. The Spaniard had worked harder than any other player on the sidelines as he repeatedly cheered, animated the crowd and offered a steady stream of thoughtful tactical advice to his teammate. He reacted to Ruud’s triumphant final smash with a jubilant scream, his legs dramatically giving way as he slid down his seat on to the ground. Alcaraz is well aware of his status as the leading star of this year’s event, and in his third Laver Cup outing, the seven-time grand slam champion at times practically took on the role of Europe’s third coach behind Yannick Noah and Tim Henman. This provided a number of insightful glimpses into the way he sees the sport. During one exchange with Ruud, Alcaraz suggested that the Norwegian should attempt more down-the-line backhands and drop shots to draw Francisco Cerundolo, his opponent, into uncomfortable positions on the court. Whether Ruud possesses the skillset to follow Alcaraz’s tactics is another question, but the reasoning he gave for those suggestions was particularly interesting: The ultimate goal, Alcaraz said, should be to “make [Cerundolo] think a little bit more.” Continue reading...

The slogan is the name of a campaign she helped to set up to protest against the illegal dumping of waste in Gospić, a town in the mountainous Lika region of central Croatia. Between 2022 and 2024, waste was illegally abandoned at several sites in the town. At one of the biggest, just 50 metres from Šikić’s home, an estimated 35,000 tonnes of waste, some of it hazardous, was dumped and buried. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘A couple of times people walked out’: how an Anne Frank musical became the hottest theater ticket of the year
data.description: The creators and stars of Slam Frank on their off-Broadway production - which reimagines the Holocaust victim as a pansexual rapper It’s difficult to not invoke the term “woke” when discussing Slam Frank , the 2025 musical that reimagines Anne Frank as a pansexual Latina. Controversial even before its first performance, it giddily satirizes identity politics through its show-within-a-show structure, in which a progressive theatre company attempts to modernize the Holocaust victim’s story by paralleling it to the struggles faced by marginalized people today. Here, the mother of “Anita” is Black, her father is neurodivergent and, while hiding in Amsterdam, they are very much immigrants. Creator Andrew Fox recognizes “a temptation to categorize it as anti-woke art”, but points readily at the show’s fans and detractors, who fall across every conceivable party line, and cautions against one-note interpretations. “I think the piece is just trying to grapple with the last 15 years of cultural and intellectual upheaval and get some comedy out of it.” Continue reading...

data.description: Catherine Corless’s exposure of almost 800 infant deaths at a home led by nuns prompted Neeson to bring the story to screen Liam Neeson still remembers his shock and shame when he read a New York Times article about the mother and baby institution in Tuam, County Galway. It was 2017 and the article chronicled the campaign by Catherine Corless , an amateur local historian, to expose abuse and neglect by Irish nuns that led to hundreds of children being buried in a mass, unmarked grave. data.title: NAZA - official trailer
data.description: Watch the official trailer for NAZA, an award-winning documentary produced by the Guardian that details the systems behind Israel’s mass killings in Gaza. The critically acclaimed film, produced with the team behind the Zone of Interest and directed by Oscar-winning film-makers Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, includes testimony from 24 Israeli military insiders, shot at night on the rooftops of Tel Aviv. Abraham and Szor are the two Israeli directors of the four behind No Other Land, which won the Oscar for best documentary in 2025. data.title: ‘In our deepest hearts we are voyeurs’: the paedophile-hunting show that inspired Robert Pattinson’s new film
data.description: Experts and insiders explain how To Catch A Predator became the most controversial show on 2000s TV A man from Long Beach, California, is here to have sex with someone he believes is a 13-year-old girl. When the journalist Chris Hansen walks in, the man’s stomach drops. He is caught, and it is the end of his life as he knew it. Hansen asks what his fate should be. “The electric chair?” he asks. No, replies Hansen. “Dateline NBC.” This is the opening scene of Primetime , a film directed by Lance Oppenheim, released in the US this week (a UK release follows on 30 October). It explores how a network news show turned sting operations into must-see television, raising a host of ethical questions about justice, voyeurism and society’s willingness to dehumanise certain offenders for profit and entertainment. Continue reading...

data.title: Add to playlist: the defiant queer dancehall of Destin Conrad and the week’s best new tracks
data.description: Every one of the Grammy-nominated Floridian’s songs reveal a different side of him. His latest album, Roadrunner, is all languid reggae basslines and come-hither lyricism From Tampa, Florida Recommended if you like Kwn, Tyla, Odeal Up next Performing in Dallas, Texas, 1 November Destin Conrad has had a busy couple of years: three albums, one Grammy nomination and a string of collaborations with fellow R&B up-and-comers such as Bellah and Nia Smith. Pick any record and you’ll hear a different side of the 26-year-old. His spring 2025 debut Love on Digital pays its dues to the genre that raised him while swerving derivative cliches with small production quirks – a vocal glitch here, a skittering Jersey beat there. Last summer’s Whimsy is a sprawling alt-jazz album that was written in two weeks , inspired by his time in a high-school jazz choir. A year later, Roadrunner arrived as a celebration of his Jamaican roots and queer identity – all languid reggae basslines, gyrating dancehall rhythms, drinks-in-the-air swagger and come-hither lyricism. Continue reading...

data.title: The best recent crime and thrillers – review roundup
data.description: Murder at the Grand Alpine Hotel by Lucy Foley; The Silent Appeal by Janice Hallett; Cold Sunset by William Boyd; The Occidental Book of the Dead by T Geronimo Johnson and The Last Tenant by Eva Björg Ægisdóttir Murder at the Grand Alpine Hotel by Lucy Foley (HarperCollins, £22) This, the first Miss Marple continuation novel, must have been a more difficult undertaking than a new Hercule Poirot; furnished by Christie with a cartoonist’s worth of exaggerated traits, the Belgian detective is surely easier to bring off the page than the unassuming but observant elderly spinster. Foley makes a commendable attempt, removing Miss Marple from the postwar austerity of St Mary Mead to the comparative luxury of the Swiss Alps. Although we are introduced to the unnamed body in the gondola cabin at the start, an immediate backward shift for a two-day lead-up means Miss Marple has little actual detecting to do until about halfway through the proceedings. Employing four narrators rather dilutes things, as well as necessitating a considerable amount of Murder of Roger Ackroyd-style withholding of information, but Foley’s Miss M shows her true colours when – of course – the hotel gets cut off from the outside world, and provides a solution worthy of the Queen of Crime herself. The Silent Appeal by Janice Hallett (Viper, £20) Bestseller Hallett’s latest novel reunites us with amateur dramatic group the Fairway Players, first encountered in her debut novel, The Appeal. This time the play is The Hollow, dramatised by Agatha Christie from her novel of the same name, and, as before, lawyers Charlotte and Femi are called upon to review the mountain of emails, online messages and police reports through which the story is told, in order to figure out exactly what happened. All we know at the start is that “a brutal murder was committed” and Hallett slowly but expertly ratchets up the tension as clashes over casting, power plays, marital suspicions and distrust of newcomers create an entire gallery of potential murderers and murderees. The epistolatory method may not be for everyone, but Hallett excels at the form – these missives are variously funny, sinister, heartfelt and thoroughly human in their relatable pettiness – and the plot is well up to her usual standard. Continue reading...

data.title: Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve review – brilliant aerial combat game fulfils the Top Gun fantasy
data.description: PlayStation 5, Xbox, PC (version played); Bandai Namco The game generates blood-pumping moments as you twist, turn and weave through the skies, while your locked-on missiles speed away to obliterate an enemy plane The core appeal of any Ace Combat game lies in the moment when the beautiful clouds part, the sunlight glints off your perfectly rendered state-of-the-art fighter jet, and guitar-shredding music kicks into overdrive as your locked-on missiles speed away to obliterate an enemy plane. All of that is 100% present in Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve. What’s new is the way it delivers its unexpectedly compelling story. Set in the Earth-like alternative world of Strangereal, where every country is absolutely obsessed with fighter planes and giant superweapons, Ace Combat drafts you into the role of a fake ace pilot called the Wings of Theve – a propaganda invention to raise the morale of a besieged nation, similar to real-life rumours about Ukraine’s Ghosts of Kyiv . You rapidly find yourself becoming an actual legendary pilot, soaring through the skies with your buddies and raining hell upon your oppressors as everybody cheers on the radio. Speaking of ghosts, you have one in your ear – your predecessor, whom nobody else can hear, a gravelly voice waxing lyrical about flying, war and whatever else is on his mind as you flit about. Continue reading...

data.title: Playing video games with my 22-year-old son has brought me to tears | Dominik Diamond
data.description: I’ve been holed up in an flat, affectionately dubbed the ‘brotel’, with my son for weeks – and we’ve revisited the first game we ever played together I have spent the last three weeks living with my 22-year-old son in a two-bedroom flat he has dubbed the ”brotel”. We cook curries and watch Lanterns . We barbecue meat and analyse Tarantino movies. We get pizza and we play video games. Boy, do we play video games! The first game I ever played in co-op with him was Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 in 2009, when he was five. He wasn’t the most accomplished sidekick, not so great at placing a mobile gun turret while under fire from what seems like a bazillion enemy soldiers, but we had a laugh. It started the video game bond between us before his sister introduced him to Banjo-Kazooie and Rayman, and he stopped being a preschool warmonger. Probably for the best. So how would it be tackling the same game nearly two decades later? Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Birdwatching is close to rapture’: Margaret Atwood on why she has given C$1m to avian research
data.description: Award-winning novelist celebrates late partner’s love of birds with gift to establish the Graeme Gibson chair in avian biology If she could be any bird, Margaret Atwood would transform into a raven. “They’re very smart. They’re social, playful and just a very successful bird,” she says while seated in a corner of a bird observatory in the Lake Erie Islands archipelago. “They’re quite an intelligent problem solver.” The observatory, which she set up with her late partner, Graeme Gibson, is located on the west shore of Pelee Island – the southernmost community in Canada – and is so new that there are no lightbulbs in a handful of lamps. data.title: Woman who accused Jay-Z of raping her aged 13 says claims were false
data.description: Unnamed woman who filed and later dropped lawsuit against rap superstar states that she never met him, contrary to initial allegation of 2000 assault A woman who accused Jay-Z of raping her when she was 13 years old has formally withdrawn her allegation, saying that she has never met the rap superstar. The unnamed woman had originally made the allegation in a lawsuit filed in 2024, claiming that Jay-Z, real name Shawn Carter, had drugged and raped her with Sean Combs, known as P Diddy. The incident was alleged to have happened at a party after an MTV awards ceremony in 2000. Continue reading...

data.title: Henry Harris’ vegetarian recipe for French onion and parsley soup
data.description: A thick and creamy, flavourful onion soup topped with grated cheese and herbs When I was a child, my mother often made onions in white sauce to serve with roast lamb. I loved their thick, velvety texture and how they brought richness, sweetness and even more savouriness to a good Sunday lunch. A similarly thick tangle of onions features in the classic soupe à l’oignon gratinée, which can’t really be mimicked without a deep, dark, beefy stock, so rather than even try, it’s best to introduce another layer of flavour entirely. The parsley here yields a very different end result that also proves to be rather comforting. Henry Harris is chef/co-owner of Bouchon Racine , London EC1. His book, The Racine Effect, is published by Quadrille at £40. To order a copy for £36, go to guardianbookshop.com Continue reading...

data.title: ‘We skate on the rooftops of damaged buildings’: a day in the life of a skateboarder in Gaza
data.description: As the war in Gaza approaches its fourth year, the Guardian follows five ordinary Palestinians as they go about their lives. Each tells the story of their day, revealing the terrible toll of the conflict. Rajab al-Reefi teaches children to skate to ‘bring some joy’, but finding boards and safe spaces is a daily challenge Rajab al-Reefi remembers the day the club’s last skateboard broke. Those pastry-thin layers of maple, carefully pressed into a curve, had carried child after child up and down the homemade ramps of the skatepark. Having endured years beyond their typical lifespan, the board’s layers buckled, cracked and finally snapped. At 30, Rajab is a leader of the Gaza skate club, a group that has spent the past decade teaching girls and boys to skate. But Israel’s siege of Gaza blocks a vast array of ordinary household goods from entering the territory, with the Israelis claiming they could be used by Hamas. One of the banned items is a skateboard. Continue reading...

data.title: The age of asterisk: Manchester City’s glittering era of success is tainted now | Barney Ronay
data.description: Friday’s verdict against Manchester City will change everything we understood about their Premier League title triumphs Welcome, then, to the age of asterisk. Whatever punishment Manchester City and their owners receive at the end of this process, the fact remains, everything is tainted now. Overturn the tables, scatter the gold coins. Throw your medals in the bin. You cheated to win them. Whatever that thing was, it’s done. Stolen glory, stolen income, stolen joy. Every chant, every “we won the lot”, every awkward documentary scene about the deep, throbbing heart of this empire of love. It all looks odd, sinister, cold, sloppy, but also, and this is always the best response, utterly absurd. Continue reading...

data.title: DN Debatt. ”Valet 2026 kommer vi att minnas som ’ingenting’-valet”
data.description: DN DEBATT. Bara 50 000 röster avgjorde till sist valet. Förvånande, anser vissa. Knappast, säger jag. Valet 2026 ägde rum i tomrummet efter valet 2022 – ingen sida har egentligen presenterat något nytt. Tidöpartierna gjorde det de sa, så deras väljare är ju nöjda. Men nya fick de inte. Oppositionen missade å sin sida öppet mål, skriver statsvetaren Love Christensen.

data.title: Zo wordt Europa overvallen door China’s verdere opmars als industriële grootmacht
data.description: De opmars van China als industriële natie raakte eerst de VS heel hard, maar pas de laatste jaren ook Europa. Industriebedrijven klagen steen en been dat ze op oneerlijke wijze weggeconcurreerd worden, bij politici breekt de paniek uit dat te veel banen verloren gaan. Wat is de China-schok 2.0, hoe is deze ontstaan en heeft Europa zitten slapen?

data.title: ‘Afpersingshoogleraar’ waarschuwt: overheden zijn kwetsbaarder voor cybercrime dan bedrijven

data.title: ‘Ik had nooit gedacht dat ik weer zou kunnen werken. Ik ben begonnen aan een nieuw hoofdstuk in mijn leven’

data.title: In ‘Tunnel Vision’ van Hofesh Shechter zoeken de dansers naar een glimpje hoop
data.description: De veelgevraagde Brits-Israëlische choreograaf Hofesh Shechter valt misschien wel enigszins in herhaling, maar ook ‘Tunnel Vision’ blijft met zijn rauwe energie en veel ruimte voor interpretatie altijd aantrekkelijk. data.title: Je moet trots zijn als je buiten de norm valt, vindt regisseur Michiel van Erp. ‘Er zijn al te veel bange homo’s’

data.title: Zastraszanie prawników będzie zwalczane na nowe sposoby
data.description: Nowa europejska konwencja zapobiegnie zastraszaniu prawników i ograniczaniu prawa do sądu. Gdy zakończy się proces jej ratyfikacji, to podobne próby łamania praworządności będą skuteczniej piętnowane – przewidują prawnicy.

data.title: Barbara Piwni: Nie chodzi o to, by pokazać, kto bardziej napiął muskuły
data.description: Destabilizacja systemu sprawiedliwości postępuje od lat. Czym się różni dążenie do tego, żeby sędziowie Trybunału Konstytucyjnego byli różnicowani ze względu na to, kto ich zgłaszał, czy ktoś ich lubi czy nie, od dzielenia sędziów na neosędziów, paleosędziów i Bóg wie jeszcze jakich sędziów? To była pierwsza odsłona tej historii. A czy ktoś dzisiaj informuje opinię publiczną, jakie są jej skutki? Rozmowa z Barbarą Piwnik, sędzią w stanie spoczynku

data.title: Szef PIP o kontrolach pracodawców: od nowego roku nie będzie taryfy ulgowej
data.description: Od 1 stycznia 2027 r. kontrole będą bardziej celowane, wtedy może się okazać, że skala nieprawidłowości w zawieraniu umów będzie zdecydowanie większa — powiedział PAP główny inspektor pracy Janusz Krasoń. Jak dodał, pracodawcy będą ponosili poważniejsze konsekwencje i „nie będzie taryfy ulgowej".

data.title: Renault wskrzesza Gordini. Legenda wraca, ale już bez ryku silnika
data.description: Dwa białe pasy wystarczyły kiedyś, by kierowcom Renault przyspieszył puls. Teraz marka sprawdza, czy zadziałają również bez dźwięku spalinowego silnika. Renault 8 Gordini Concept ma 270 KM, napęd na tylne koła i wygląd, który budzi apetyt na jazdę. Na razie jednak przygotowuje się na salon w Paryżu, a nie do produkcji.

data.title: Baza USA w Polsce. Znamy wstępne koszty i jej liczebność
data.description: Stałą bazę wojsk USA w Polsce już w 2029 roku może otworzyć Donald Trump – dowiedziała się „Rzeczpospolita”. O sukcesie przedsięwzięcia zadecyduje amerykańska decyzja o sile i rodzaju sił zbrojnych zgrupowanych w naszym kraju oraz tempo prac w polskim rządzie nad specustawą. Wsparcie w tych pracach deklaruje prezydent Karol Nawrocki.

data.title: Itálie zavádí limit počtu žáků, kteří neumí italsky. Ve školách zakáže i zahalování
data.description: Italská vláda ve čtvrtek schválila dekret, jímž ve třídách omezuje počet žáků, kteří nemají dostatečnou znalost italštiny. Takových bude moci být v každé třídě nejvýše 30 procent. Dekret také ve školách zakazuje nošení šátků zakrývajících obličej. Podle italské vlády je cílem nových pravidel posílit integraci.

data.title: Suché lesy na Vysočině zkropil déšť, sběrači spěchají na hřiby
data.description: Po několikaměsíční abstinenci mají milovníci houbaření svoji „drogu“ opět na dosah. A je znát, že jim chyběla. Sotva Vysočinu zkropily po suchých měsících první kapky deště, zaplnily se příjezdové cesty do lesů auty. Také sociální sítě se hemží snímky úlovků. Národ houbařů je v pohotovosti.

data.title: Lebka svaté Zdislavy čeká na uložení, nahradí ji relikviář s ostatkem
data.description: Nedávno ukradená lebka svaté Zdislavy bude v budoucnu uložena s ostatními ostatky, které jsou v kryptě baziliky v Jablonném v Podještědí na Liberecku. V bazilice samotné bude na původním místě lebky nový relikviář, ve kterém bude malý ostatek světice, takže úcta k ní zůstane zachována.

data.title: Ústí nepotřebuje obří projekty, ale čisté ulice, tvrdí lídryně Ústečáků Nechybová
data.description: Bývalá primátorka a současná náměstkyně primátora Ústí nad Labem Věra Nechybová jde do komunálních voleb jako lídryně kandidátky Ústečáků. data.title: Nákupy kartou prolomily nový rekord. A co by si drtivá většina lidí přála nejvíc
data.description: Češi při nakupování dávají přednost platební kartě před hotovostí. Preference digitálních plateb vzrostla na rekordních 61 procent a 80 procent Čechů by kartou platilo při každém nákupu, pokud by tato možnost byla všude k dispozici. Vyplývá to z aktuálního průzkumu společnosti Mastercard mezi 1 212 respondenty.

data.title: Město musí požadovat u nové výstavby co největší parkoviště, říká olomoucký lídr SPD
data.description: Hnutí SPD prožívá nejúspěšnější politické období ve své historii, poprvé usedlo ve vedení kraje, navíc je též prvně součástí vládní koalice. Přesun z opozičních lavic by teď rádo zopakovalo také v olomouckém zastupitelstvu. „Děláme vše pro to, abychom měli dvojciferný výsledek a mohli se zapojit do vedení města,“ říká lídr společné kandidátky SPD, Trikolory a Svobodných Pavel Jelínek.

data.title: Čínská první dáma poutá pozornost. S Melanií mluvila anglicky bez tlumočníka
data.description: Čínská první dáma Peng Liyuan ve Washingtonu upoutala pozornost svou angličtinou. Při setkání s Melanií Trumpovou si podle záběrů z návštěvy krátce povídala bez viditelné pomoci tlumočníka. Peng Liyuanová se během návštěvy objevila také po boku místního mládežnického sboru, kterému poděkovala za vystoupení v čínštině.

data.title: Napětí na hranici s Afghánistánem. Provázel ho pákistánský letecký útok

data.title: "Tudo começou com pedras talhadas". Arqueóloga Sara Cura revela como a pré-história inventou o mundo moderno
data.description: Porque devemos procurar as origens da inovação milhares de anos antes do aparecimento da escrita? Algumas respostas podem ser encontradas no livro da arqueóloga Sara Cura, lançado recentemente. Ao percorrer 3,5 milhões de anos da pré-história, a investigadora mostra como a necessidade aguçou o engenho e a criatividade humanos, demonstrando que muitas das grandes inovações nasceram nas comunidades de caçadores-recoletores e perduraram até aos nossos dias.

data.description: Yaoundé (Cameroun) – 24 septembre 2026 — Réunis au Palais de Verre de l’Assemblée nationale du Cameroun du 22 au 24 septembre 2026, les parlementaires d’Afrique centrale, accompagnés de représentants gouvernementaux, de chercheurs et d’organisations internationales, ont adopté à l’unanimité la Déclaration finale de Yaoundé. Cette rencontre de haut niveau marque un tournant stratégique pour la préservation des forêts du Bassin du Congo et l'accès équitable aux financements climatiques mondiaux.

data.title: Climat et gouvernance forestière en Afrique centrale : Mettre la science et le leadership parlementaire au service du bassin du Congo
data.description: Yaoundé, 22 septembre 2026 - La Conférence parlementaire sur la science, la gouvernance environnementale et la finance climatique en Afrique Centrale s'est ouverte ce jour à l'Assemblée Nationale du Cameroun à Yaoundé. Organisé par le Réseau des Parlementaires pour la Gestion Durable des Écosystèmes Forestiers d'Afrique Centrale (REPAR) avec l'appui de l'Observatoire des Forêts d'Afrique Centrale (OFAC), de la COMIFAC, de Landscape Alliance (CIFOR-ICRAF) et le soutien financier de l'Union européenne à travers le projet OFAC-CE, cet événement majeur rassemble des parlementaires de toute la sous-région, des ministres, des banques de développement, des scientifiques et des partenaires techniques et financiers.

data.title: Cameroun : D-Clic forme 160 jeunes à l’emploi et l’auto-emploi
data.description: © JDC La remise des attestations de la session 2026 du programme D-Clic <<Formez-vous au numérique avec l'OIF>>, le 24 septembre 2026 a marqué la fin de quatre mois de formation de 160 jeunes au sein du centre TechLab Academy. Sur 180 candidats retenus au départ, 160 ont suivi l'intégralité de la formation. A l'issue du cursus, 105 ont obtenu une attestation de réussite et 55 repartent avec une attestation de participation. Les lauréats ont bénéficié des connaissances dans cinq parcours professionnalisants. Entre autres, Décoration d'intérieur, Électronique embarquée IOT, impression et broderie textile, Création visuelle. Les bénéficiaires du programme ont conçu et livré une soixantaine de projets réels commandés par des clients externes, allant de la fabrication de mobilier modulable local à la conception de prototypes électroniques de détection de fuites de gaz domestique. La filière création visuelle a le plus suscité l'intérêt. Les apprenants ont fait une démonstration de leur maîtrise des logiciels 2D/3D et de découpe laser au CNC. Également la réalisation collective d'un totem lumineux de 4,50 mètres de haut pour une entreprise. <<Nous voulons montrer que les femmes peuvent exercer dans ce secteur, décrocher des marchés et devenir les entrepreneurs de demain>>, affirme Alexia Abia, bénéficiaire. Kibila Duc, apprenant de nationalité congolaise, formé en décoration d'intérieur confie : << mon objectif est de créer mon entreprise et de structurer cette filière dans mon pays où elle n'existe pas encore.>> Le représentant du ministère de la Formation professionnelle a réitéré l'engagement du gouvernement à promouvoir les métiers émergents et a lancé un appel aux acteurs économiques pour accompagner les bénéficiaires vers l'emploi et l'auto-emploi. Cet article Cameroun : D-Clic forme 160 jeunes à l’emploi et l’auto-emploi est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Cameroun/ Électricité : l’ARSEL et la Banque mondiale s’accordent sur les priorités d’investissement
data.description: © DR Le mardi 22 septembre 2026, l'Agence de régulation du secteur de l'electricité a reçu une équipe de la Banque mondiale à son siège. Objectif : préparer un nouveau programme d'investissement pour améliorer la performance du système électrique camerounais, avec trois axes prioritaires retenus. La performance du système électrique au cœur des échanges. Le mardi 22 septembre 2026, au siège de l'ARSEL, l'Agence de Régulation du Secteur de l'Électricité a tenu une séance de concertation avec une équipe de la Banque mondiale, dans le cadre de la préparation d'un nouveau programme d'investissement dans le secteur de l'énergie. Au cœur des échanges, les projets susceptibles de contribuer à l'amélioration de la performance du système électrique, notamment l'étude du coût du service et la tarification de l'électricité, la gestion dynamique de la demande (« demand response ») pour mieux équilibrer l'offre et la demande, et le relèvement du facteur de puissance afin d'optimiser l'utilisation des capacités disponibles. Les discussions ont également porté sur la réduction des pertes dans le réseau de distribution, l'amélioration des outils de prévision de la demande et le renforcement des capacités de planification et de régulation. À l'issue de la rencontre, trois axes ont été retenus comme prioritaires pour la première phase : coût du service et tarification, gestion de la demande et relèvement du facteur de puissance. Une concertation qui traduit la volonté commune de renforcer la performance, l'efficacité et la durabilité du secteur de l'électricité au Cameroun. Cet article Cameroun/ Électricité : l’ARSEL et la Banque mondiale s’accordent sur les priorités d’investissement est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Journée mondiale du gorille : le WWF et le MINFOF sensibilisent les élèves de Salapoumbé
data.description: © DR À l'occasion de la Journée mondiale du gorille célébrée le 24 septembre, le WWF - Programme Jengi TNS, en partenariat avec le Ministère des Forêts et de la Faune, a organisé une journée de sensibilisation à Salapoumbé, dans la région de l'Est, à l'intention des élèves. Protéger le gorille pour préserver la forêt. À l'occasion de la Journée mondiale du gorille, célébrée le 24 septembre, le WWF - Programme Jengi TNS, en partenariat avec le MINFOF, a organisé une journée de sensibilisation auprès des élèves de Salapoumbé, dans la région de l'Est. Au programme, des échanges pédagogiques sur l'importance des gorilles, espèce emblématique du bassin du Congo, et sur la nécessité de protéger leur habitat, de plus en plus menacé par le braconnage et la déforestation. Les activités se sont poursuivies par des séances de plantation d'arbres avec les élèves, geste symbolique et concret en faveur de la restauration des écosystèmes. À travers ces actions, le WWF et le MINFOF entendent encourager les jeunes à mieux comprendre, protéger et préserver la biodiversité qui les entoure, et à devenir des ambassadeurs de la conservation au sein de leurs communautés. Une initiative qui s'inscrit dans les efforts de conservation du paysage transfrontalier Tri-National de la Sangha. Cet article Journée mondiale du gorille : le WWF et le MINFOF sensibilisent les élèves de Salapoumbé est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Cobalt-nickel de Nkamouna : le groupe américain ARM annonce 85 millions de dollars d’investissement
data.description: © DR L'entreprise américaine ARM, basée à Washington D.C., est en discussions avancées pour le développement du projet cobalt-nickel-manganèse de Nkamouna, situé dans l'arrondissement de Lomié, département du Haut-Nyong, région de l'Est. Un investissement initial de 85 millions de dollars est prévu avec une mise en production dans les 18 mois. Le partenariat minier entre Yaoundé et Washington se renforce. ARM, entreprise spécialisée dans les minéraux stratégiques dont le siège est à Washington D.C., mène des discussions en vue de conclure un accord pour le développement du gisement polymétallique de Nkamouna, localité située dans l'arrondissement de Lomié, département du Haut-Nyong, région de l'Est. Cet accord prévoit un investissement initial d'environ 85 millions de dollars dans une première usine de traitement modulaire sur le site minier, avec une mise en production prévue dans les 18 mois suivant l'entrée en vigueur du permis, ainsi que des investissements supplémentaires dans des modules additionnels. ARM apporte son expertise en traitement des minerais, sa capacité de financement et son expérience mondiale. L'initiative bénéficie de capitaux américains, du soutien du gouvernement des États-Unis et d'un engagement en faveur d'un développement responsable, en partenariat avec le Cameroun et une entreprise locale. Le gisement de Nkamouna, considéré comme l'un des plus prometteurs d'Afrique centrale pour le cobalt et le nickel, est au cœur de la stratégie des métaux critiques pour la transition énergétique. Cet article Cobalt-nickel de Nkamouna : le groupe américain ARM annonce 85 millions de dollars d’investissement est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Plan de Convergence COMIFAC 2026-2035 : le CIDP prend part à la validation à Yaoundé
data.description: © DR Invité au Forum sous-régional de validation du Plan de Convergence 2026-2035 de la COMIFAC, le Conseil International de Dialogue et de Partenariat (CIDP) a pris part aux travaux tenus les 17 et 18 septembre 2026 au siège de la Commission des Forêts d'Afrique Centrale à Yaoundé. Un plan ambitieux à 7 milliards USD par an pour les forêts, le climat et la biodiversité. La COMIFAC peaufine sa vision 2035. Le CIDP était au rendez-vous du Forum sous-régional de validation du 3e Plan de Convergence (PC3), tenu les 17 et 18 septembre 2026 au siège de la COMIFAC à Yaoundé. Deux jours de travaux autour d'un plan directeur articulé en trois volets : un cadre stratégique avec une vision 2035, 4 axes stratégiques et 36 cibles ; un plan opérationnel 2026-2030 avec l'ambition de porter à 7 milliards USD par an les financements pour les forêts, le climat et la biodiversité ; et un cadre de gouvernance, de performance et de redevabilité. Parmi les innovations du PC3 : l'approche « Une Seule Santé » (One Health), la place accordée aux jeunes, aux femmes et aux communautés locales, l'usage de l'intelligence artificielle et de la télédétection pour l'alerte précoce, et le renforcement de la diplomatie environnementale. Pour le CIDP, cette participation est l'occasion de contribuer à ce plan directeur pour l'environnement en Afrique centrale et de réaffirmer son engagement en faveur de l'approche One Health et de la diplomatie environnementale, au service de la préservation des forêts du bassin du Congo. Cet article Plan de Convergence COMIFAC 2026-2035 : le CIDP prend part à la validation à Yaoundé est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Diamond Capital Convention 2026 : le MINFI appelle à orienter les capitaux vers l’économie réelle
data.description: © DR Réunis à Douala pour la première édition de la Diamond Capital Convention le 24 septembre 2026, les acteurs de la finance ont débattu de la mobilisation des capitaux. Présidant l'ouverture, le Ministre des Finances Louis Paul Motaze a plaidé pour un marché financier plus profond et attractif au service des entreprises et des projets structurants du Cameroun et de la CEMAC. Faire de la finance un levier de transformation. Réunis à Douala le 24 septembre 2026 à l'occasion de la première édition de la Diamond Capital Convention 2026, les principaux acteurs de l'écosystème financier ont échangé sur les moyens de mobiliser davantage de capitaux en faveur de l'économie réelle. Présidant la cérémonie d'ouverture, le Ministre des Finances, Louis Paul Motaze, a mis en avant la nécessité de développer un marché financier plus profond, dynamique et attractif, capable d'accompagner les entreprises, les infrastructures et les grands projets de transformation économique du Cameroun et de la CEMAC. Pour le Minfi, l'enjeu est clair : canaliser l'épargne longue vers les secteurs productifs, renforcer la confiance des investisseurs et améliorer les mécanismes de financement des PME, trop souvent exclues du circuit bancaire classique. Cette première édition, qui se veut une plateforme de réflexion et de mise en relation entre investisseurs, émetteurs, régulateurs et entrepreneurs, intervient dans un contexte de besoin accru en financements pour l'industrialisation et les infrastructures. Le Ministre a ainsi appelé à accélérer les réformes, à innover dans les instruments financiers et à renforcer l'éducation financière pour bâtir un marché des capitaux au service de la croissance inclusive. Cet article Diamond Capital Convention 2026 : le MINFI appelle à orienter les capitaux vers l’économie réelle est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Développement local à l’Est : Bélabo montre l’exemple et rafle la distinction de meilleure commune
data.description: © DR Le Conseil municipal a été sacré meilleure commune de la région par Plan International pour son modèle de gestion participative et ses réalisations communautaires, lors d'une cérémonie officielle riche en symboles, sanctionnée par une enveloppe de 2 000 000 FCFA. C'est une consécration pour tout un arrondissement. Le Conseil municipal de Bélabo vient d'être distingué comme la commune la plus performante de la région de l'Est, à l’occasion d’une cérémonie solennelle organisée par Plan International Cameroon, laquelle a réuni les autorités administratives, traditionnelles et religieuses, les partenaires sectoriels, les groupes de jeunes et les populations locales. Au-delà du chèque symbolique de 2 000 000 FCFA remis à cette occasion, c'est tout le modèle de gouvernance locale de Bélabo qui est salué. Pour le Maire, Emmanuel Apande, cette récompense est le fruit d'un effort commun. La distinction honore la commune et récompense le travail collectif mené avec dévouement, responsabilité, transparence et solidarité. La gestion de la municipalité a été jugée efficace en particulier dans la mise en œuvre des projets communautaires visant à améliorer durablement le bien-être des enfants et des familles. Les communautés au cœur du développement Le secret de Bélabo est de faire confiance aux populations. Le modèle mis en avant place les communautés au premier plan : ce sont elles qui identifient leurs priorités et qui conduisent elles-mêmes les initiatives de développement. Une approche qui, selon les organisateurs, vise aussi à créer une saine émulation entre les communes, pour que chacune soit motivée à donner le meilleur d'elle-même pour sa population et à changer positivement le récit du développement local. Avec des réalisations concrètes et visibles dans les villages, Bélabo apporte la preuve qu'un autre développement est possible. Lorsque les communautés locales sont responsabilisées et habilitées à prendre en main leur propre avenir, le changement durable n'est plus une utopie, il devient réalité. Bélabo s'impose désormais comme une référence et un modèle à suivre pour le développement local dans la région de l'Est, d’après Plan international Cameroon. Cet article Développement local à l’Est : Bélabo montre l’exemple et rafle la distinction de meilleure commune est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Affaire des lunettes du ministre : L’UDC exige des excuses publiques et réparation pour les quatre journalistes humiliés
data.description: © DR L'affaire des quatre journalistes interpellés pour le vol présumé des lunettes du ministre de l’Economie, de la Planification et de l’Aménagement du Territoire Alamine Ousmane Mey prend une tournure politique. L’UDC y voit une autre forme d’atteinte à la démocratie. Dans une déclaration officielle signée de son président national, le maire Hermine Patricia Tomaino Ndam Njoya, l'Union démocratique du Cameroun (UDC) ne mâche pas ses mots. Elle exige clairement la réparation du préjudice subi par les journalistes ainsi que des excuses publiques. Pour le parti du regretté Adamou Ndam Njoya, l'incident survenu les 16 et 17 septembre 2026 en marge des Journées de la Banque islamique de développement au Palais des Congrès est "aussi insolite que fâcheux, car des plus dégradant". L'Union démocratique du Cameroun se demande comment on peut comprendre que des journalistes en plein exercice de leur métier soient confondus avec de vulgaires voleurs. Qu'ils soient à la va-vite aussi facilement jetés en cellule et à la vindicte populaire. La formation politique rappelle le fait le plus accablant : selon les déclarations des victimes, les lunettes auraient été retrouvées dès le 17 septembre à l'intérieur même du véhicule du ministre, alors que les journalistes François Essomba, Igor Gwet Bibey, Solange Djuikam et Pierre Mouchili sont restés en garde à vue au commissariat central n°1 jusqu'au 21 septembre, dans des "conditions de tristes renommées". Dénonçant un tel traitement, le parti énonce cinq exigences : il rappelle que la presse, Quatrième pouvoir, mérite considération. S’indigne de la "clochardisation de nos Médias" par le régime. Réaffirme son engagement pour une presse fière et libre. Exprime sa désolation aux quatre victimes. Et surtout, demande que réparation soit faite et que des excuses publiques soient présentées. La position de l’UDC qui rejoint celle du Syndicat national des professionnels de l’information et de la communication –SPIC- qui, reçu mercredi par le ministre de la Communication René Sadi, avait déjà jugé les excuses publiques "non négociables". Pourtant, le ministre de l’Economie a fait une déclaration tendant redonner aux professionnels de la presse leur position. Une déclaration du ministre jugée insuffisante Sorti de son silence, le ministre Alamine Ousmane Mey a déclaré : « À propos des médias, j'ai une très grande estime pour la profession. J'ai du respect pour les journalistes qui en assument la responsabilité. Rien ne pourra réduire cette estime à la dimension physique d'une paire de lunettes, encore moins à sa valeur vénale. » Une phrase qui se veut apaisante, mais qui pour de nombreux observateurs et pour l'UDC, ne suffit pas. Car derrière les mots, il reste 5 jours de cellule, une humiliation publique et des journalistes sous observation médicale pendant 21 jours. Pour une paire de lunettes retrouvée dans la voiture du ministre lui-même, les professionnels attendent mieux qu'une formule : ils attendent des actes, une réparation et de vraies excuses publiques. Cet article Affaire des lunettes du ministre : L’UDC exige des excuses publiques et réparation pour les quatre journalistes humiliés est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Vêtuste et enclavée, Lusambo peine à assumer son statut de chef-lieu de province de Sankuru
data.description: Sur instruction de la Première ministre, plusieurs régies financières et services publics dont la DGI, la DGRAD, la DGDA et la Banque centrale du Congo doivent être délocalisés de Lodja vers Lusambo. Toutefois, le chef-lieu du Sankuru fait face à un état de délabrement avancé de ses infrastructures publiques, héritées pour la plupart de l'époque coloniale et inadaptées aux besoins administratifs actuels.

data.title: Young Positivist Writes : My Experience with GCLP
data.description:
Folks, in a cautious effort to raise awareness of climate change and its effects on humans and ecosystems, I have decided to talk about another important aspect of climate change: climate education. In this piece, I will discuss the Ghana Climate Literacy Portal (GCLP), how it has shaped my understanding and perspective on climate change, and how it has recently inspired me to contribute to my climate-change write-ups. 

Climate change is an important matter that needs to be taken seriously, and climate education is equally essential. Climate education empowers citizens to take meaningful action. Climate change affects everyone. It does not discriminate based on whether someone knows about it or not.

data.title: Strong Day 1 turnout sets tone for Day 2 of Republic Bank-JoyNews Habitat Fair Clinic
data.description:
Strong patronage on the opening day of the third Republic Bank-JoyNews Habitat Fair Clinic has set the tone for a busy second day, as prospective homeowners and property investors return to the Junction Mall in Nungua to explore housing and financing solutions.

The three-day clinic, which opened on Friday, September 25, attracted patrons who engaged exhibitors on mortgage financing, property investment, home construction, furnishing, security, and other housing-related services.

Day 2 of the event continues today, Saturday, September 26, with exhibitors on hand to provide information and answer questions from prospective homeowners and investors looking to buy, build or improve their homes.

data.title: Ghana Army warns new soldiers against social media misuse, uniform abuse
data.description:
The Ghana Army has cautioned newly trained soldiers against misusing social media and the military uniform, urging them to uphold the reputation of the Ghana Armed Forces (GAF) and obey the laws of Ghana.

The warning was issued at the passing-out parade of 646 recruits of the Basic Infantry Training Course (BITC) 1-26 at the Army Recruit Training School (ARTS) at Shai Hills in the Greater Accra Region on Friday, September 25, 2026.

The recruits reported for training on March 27 and underwent six months of intensive instruction in physical training, drill, tactics, weapon handling, fieldcraft, map reading, military law and first aid.

Reviewing Officer and General Officer Commanding (GOC) of the Southern Command, Brigadier General Edward Awaribey, said 650 recruits commenced the course, but four were unable to complete the training for medical and disciplinary reasons.

data.title: AMA calls for science-led action to tackle environmental health risks in Accra
data.description:
The Accra Metropolitan Assembly (AMA) has called for stronger use of scientific evidence in shaping policies and enforcement measures to address environmental health risks in the metropolis.

The call was made as the AMA joined communities around the world to mark World Environmental Health Day on Saturday, September 26, under the theme “Environmental Health: Standing with Science to Protect Communities.”

The Assembly, through its Metro Public Health Department, said Accra continues to face environmental health challenges linked to poor sanitation, unsafe food handling, waste pollution, flooding, air pollution and rising temperatures.

The AMA said addressing these risks requires evidence-based policies backed by effective enforcement and practical action at the community level.

data.title: He entered at eight; he is now 16: Ghana’s children growing up in prayer camps
data.description:
At eight years old, Hafiz Abdallah was taken to Nyinbonya, a prayer camp in Paga, near Ghana’s border with Burkina Faso.

He is now 16.

For eight years, his mother says, her son has lived at the facility without a clinical diagnosis.

When his behaviour becomes erratic, she says, he is chained.

“He doesn't even speak, stands often in his own world,” she said. “But this helped me a lot because I am very much assured that he will not wander off and end up getting hurt or killed.”

Hafiz became increasingly difficult to manage after the death of his twin brother. He destroyed things, once stole a neighbour's chicken and often attacked his mother.

data.title: ‘Development must not always begin from Accra’ — Anwelle Foundation launched in Jirapa
data.description:
The Paramount Chief of the Jirapa Traditional Area, Naa Di-Naa Donlabong III, has called on residents and natives of Jirapa living outside the community to take greater responsibility for its development instead of relying solely on government.

He made the call at the launch of the Anwelle Foundation in Jirapa in the Upper West Region, where he urged citizens to bring their resources, expertise and networks home to help tackle poverty and youth unemployment.

“Development does not always have to begin from Accra. It can begin here. It can begin from a young man who refuses to give up on his community; it can begin from a woman farmer, a teacher, a student, a philanthropist, or from the traditional palace. And sometimes, it can begin with nothing more than a decision to care,” Naa Di-Naa Donlabong III said.

The foundation is focused on addressing resource gaps in rural communities through interventions in education, youth empowerment, sustainable livelihoods and rural development.

The Paramount Chief said sustainable development required communities to look beyond government for solutions and encouraged sons and daughters of Jirapa across the world to return with their capital, academic knowledge, professional expertise and networks.

data.title: JoyNews gets results as listeners raise GH¢40,000 to help 17-year-old student with cerebral palsy attend SHS
data.description:
Seventeen-year-old Priscilla Nana Ama Samson, a student living with cerebral palsy, has returned to senior high school after Ghanaians rallied to support her education.

Priscilla had feared she would be unable to resume school because her mother could not afford the items listed on her school prospectus.

Her situation was highlighted by JoyNews, prompting an overwhelming response from listeners and members of the public.

About GH¢40,000 has since been raised to help Priscilla meet her school-related needs and return to the classroom.

data.title: Vice President calls for stronger local pharmaceutical production to reduce medicine imports
data.description:
Vice President Professor Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang has called for stronger local pharmaceutical production as Ghana seeks to reduce its reliance on imported medicines and improve access to essential drugs.

She said expanding the capacity of Ghanaian pharmaceutical manufacturers would strengthen the health system and help the country respond more effectively to changing healthcare needs.

The Vice President was speaking in Accra at the opening of the 90th Anniversary Annual General Meeting and Scientific Conference of the Pharmaceutical Society of Ghana.

data.title: The brewing tension at KNUST; Beware the Ides of October….
data.description:
Less than a month after the investiture of a new Vice-Chancellor, the Governing Council of KNUST has decided to end a practice that has been part of KNUST's academic governance for generations: faculty will no longer elect their own Deans and Pro-Vice-Chancellors. They will be appointed.

The timing alone should make everyone pause. A new administration has barely settled in, and already one of the University's longest-standing traditions of academic participation is being dismantled. Even more troubling is that Council is proceeding despite formal petitions from the major recognized staff unions, UTAG, GAUA and TEWU-TUC, strongly opposing the change. These are not peripheral voices; they represent the staff whose participation in the governance of the University is now being removed. 

It is therefore much bigger than a change in procedure; it is a transfer of power from the academic community to the centre.

data.title: Discours en malgache à l'ONU : aucune infraction aux règles onusiennes
data.description: L'utilisation de la langue malgache par le colonel Randrianirina lors de son premier discours devant l'Assemblée générale de l'Organisation des Nations unies (AG-ONU) a entraîné beaucoup de réactions. Sans commentaire sur le contenu de son allocution ou la personne de l'intervenant, rappelons que la liste des six langues officielles et langues de travail de l'AG-ONU est définie dans les articles 51 et 52 de son règlement intérieur : l'anglais, l'arabe, le chinois, l'espagnol, le français (…) - Editorial

data.title: El que persevera triunfa: la carrera de resistencia de Anisleidis Ochoa, la Polaca (+ Fotos e Infografías)
data.description: Hubo un momento en que Anisleidis Ochoa quiso dejar de correr. No veía futuro en aquellas madrugadas, en los kilómetros interminables ni en una pista que parecía exigirle más de lo que podía dar. Entonces apareció su madre y le dijo, en esencia, que volviera a intentarlo. Años después, aquella niña que pensó en abandonar terminaría coleccionando medallas, rompiendo récords y llevando un apodo que nació casi por casualidad: “la Polaca”. data.title: Dentro de la incursión armada desde Florida destinada a derrocar al gobierno de Cuba
data.description: LA HABANA, Cuba—El pasado mes de noviembre, José Manuel Rodríguez Castelló, un camionero de 33 años, estaba navegando por TikTok cuando se topó con un vídeo en directo publicado por Raúl Quevedo, un cubano que vive en Estados Unidos. Habían pasado casi diez años desde que Rodríguez emigró a Estados Unidos desde Cuba con una visa de prometido. Posteriormente obtuvo la residencia permanente y vivía con su novia y la hija de ella en Nashville, Tennessee. Sin embargo, albergaba un profundo resentimiento hacia lo que consideraba un gobierno dictatorial que reprimía al pueblo cubano, y se alegró de ver que Quevedo lo denunciaba. La cuenta de Quevedo, La Nueva Cuba , está repleta de imágenes que representan la resistencia armada y una Cuba poscomunista imaginaria, muchas de ellas generadas por IA. Rodríguez le envió un mensaje a Quevedo, quien le respondió. Congeniaron de inmediato, y Rodríguez contó que Quevedo lo invitó a Florida para conocer a un grupo de exiliados con ideas afines. “Buscaban personas que tuvieran el valor de unirse a un levantamiento armado en Cuba”, dijo Rodríguez. Medio año después, Rodríguez estaría en La Habana, explicando a un periodista cómo había terminado bajo custodia cubana, pero firme en su determinación de derrocar  » The post Dentro de la incursión armada desde Florida destinada a derrocar al gobierno de Cuba first appeared on Cubadebate .
